forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Oxford's service risk register scores housing demand at 15, with overspends that "risk the financial stability" of the council
news_drafts.lead:
Oxford City Council's service risk register, presented to its Audit and Governance Committee on 27 October 2026, gives its highest score to housing demand: 15, from a probability of 3 and an impact of 5. The register describes the risk as "overspends of a scale that risk the financial stability of the Council".

The register says the risk covers rising rents, changes to eligibility and homelessness demand, which increase the number of temporary accommodation placements and their cost. It rates the overall impact as one that could undermine the council's ability to perform its statutory functions and remain financially stable.

Two other risks sit in the same register. Legal services is scored 12 (probability 4, impact 3). The register says that "as unexpected corporate issues arise, external legal costs increase, which will lead to an overspend on the legal services budget". It links this to capacity issues and to the council being unable to use its usual procurement route, the EM Lawshare Framework, which means using higher-priced frameworks. The consequence it records is budgetary pressure.

Capital receipts, the money from selling assets, is scored 4 (probability 2, impact 2). The register attributes this to market forces and dependence on third parties, and links it to sales from the investment portfolio, which would reduce income. It says reduced capital "causes increased borrowing or reduction in capital programme", the council's planned spending on things that last, such as buildings and equipment.

news_drafts.headline: Oxford tower block fire safety project spent just £169k of £6.56m budget
news_drafts.lead: Oxford City Council spent only £169,080 of a £6.56 million budget for mandatory fire safety work on tower blocks in the year to March 2026, according to accounts submitted to Cabinet on 16 September. The project involved replacing fire alarm systems to meet fire safety requirements. The underspend of £6.39 million—representing 97 per cent of the approved budget—suggests either the project was severely delayed into the following financial year, the budget was drastically misjudged, or the work was not undertaken as planned. The council has not explained the discrepancy in the papers.

findings.paper_title: 26 OxCity LG Reserve Risk Assessment Report - Final
findings.headline: EY links the timing of the historic assurance rebuild to upcoming Local Government Reorganisation
findings.detail: EY says that avoiding further delay in rebuilding assurance over the Council's historic position is essential, and that the timing is critical because of upcoming Local Government Reorganisation.
findings.matters: Reorganisation timing affects how and when historic reserve balances are assured, which matters to any council or lender working through a reorganisation.
findings.quote: which is critical given the timing of upcoming Local Government Reorganisation

findings.paper_title: 26 OxCity LG Reserve Risk Assessment Report - Final
findings.headline: EY will seek a variation to its scale fee for the reserves risk assessment and the historical assurance rebuild
findings.detail: EY says the risk assessment, the preparation of the MHCLG submission and the drafting of the addendum are outside the scale fee. Procedures to rebuild historical assurance will also fall outside it, and EY will report the agreed costs later.
findings.matters: Additional audit fees for historic rebuild work are a cost a finance director must budget for, and the amount is not yet known.
findings.figures: None stated; the cost has not yet been agreed
findings.quote: we will seek a variation to the scale fee to reflect these changes to the scope of our work

findings.paper_title: 26 OxCity LG Reserve Risk Assessment Report - Final
findings.headline: EY says the Council's progress 'falls behind' the expected LARRIG 01 timescales for rebuilding audit assurance
findings.detail: The paper compares the Council's progress with the illustrative timeline in the NAO's LARRIG 01 guidance and concludes that it is behind. EY states that the natural rebuild must start before the historic gaps can be addressed.
findings.matters: A council that is behind the national reset timeline is a useful reference point for other councils assessing where they stand against the same guidance.
findings.quote: In our view, the Council's progress falls behind the expected timescales set out in LARRIG 01.

findings.paper_title: 26 OxCity LG Reserve Risk Assessment Report - Final
findings.headline: Assurance could not be obtained over elements of the Capital Financing Requirement in the 2024/25 audit
findings.detail: The paper says the shortfall relates to capital debtors and capital leases. EY links this to the Capital Adjustment Account and the Capital Receipts Reserve, both of which are rated Significant Risk.
findings.matters: The Capital Financing Requirement drives borrowing headroom, so unverified elements matter to lenders and to finance directors assessing capital financing capacity.
findings.quote: assurance could not be obtained over certain elements of the Capital Financing Requirement due to insufficient supporting evidence for capital debtors and capital leases.

findings.paper_title: 26 OxCity LG Reserve Risk Assessment Report - Final
findings.headline: A 2024/25 prior-year adjustment restated the Capital Grants Unapplied Account by £16.8 million, relating to grant income timing
findings.detail: EY reports that the adjustment arose from the timing of grant income recognition. Combined with the significant weakness reported, this leads EY to rate the Capital Grants Unapplied Account as a Significant Risk.
findings.matters: A restatement of this size in grant accounting is a concrete example of the misstatement risk that other councils with grant-funded capital programmes should consider.
findings.quote: a prior-year adjustment identified during the 2024/25 audit resulted in a £16.8 million restatement associated with the timing of grant income recognition.
